name: Broadcom Inc.

sections.title: Quarterly revenue
sections.callout: Outlook: Broadcom guided Q1 FY2026 revenue to about $19.1B, including about $8.2B of AI semiconductor revenue, roughly double a year earlier.

tiles.label: Share repurchases
tiles.foot: Program only; excludes $3.9B withheld for taxes

footnotes: Broadcom recorded a $0.4B net income tax benefit in FY2025, including a one-time $2.1B benefit, so net income exceeds pre-tax income; the flow chart shows pre-tax income flowing to net income.
Fiscal 2025 ended Nov 2, 2025; fiscal 2026 results were not yet filed. Free cash flow as reported by Broadcom.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Broadcom's revenue grew 23.9% to $63.9B in fiscal 2025 (ended November 2, 2025). Semiconductor solutions rose 22.5% to $36.9B, driven by AI chips, and infrastructure software rose 25.8% to $27.0B. Operating income nearly doubled to $25.5B.
Net income nearly quadrupled to $23.1B, or $4.77 per diluted share, helped by a tax benefit. Free cash flow rose 38.6% to $26.9B, and Broadcom paid $11.1B in dividends.
highlights: Q4 FY2025 revenue reached a record $18.0B, up 28.2%.
Operating margin rose to 39.9% from 26.1% as VMware-related amortization and restructuring costs fell.
Q1 FY2026 guidance calls for about $8.2B of AI semiconductor revenue, roughly double a year earlier.
watch: Total debt remains high at $65.1B, though it fell 3.6%.
Net income was lifted by a one-time $2.1B tax benefit.
Amortization of acquired intangibles still cost $8.1B across cost of revenue and operating expenses.
sources: Broadcom Q4 and fiscal year 2025 results

revenueLine.cap: Semiconductors were 58% of revenue and software 42%; both grew over 20%.
revenueLine.say: Semiconductor solutions made up 58 percent of revenue and infrastructure software 42 percent, and both grew more than 20 percent.
